name: Romance Stories
purpose: A starting subject map for a Romance Stories YouTube channel. Categories organize concrete subtopics; each entry supplies an episode question, a research outline and a boundary for case selection. Counts follow the authored coverage, with no imposed topic maximum.

topics.title: Friends negotiating changed feelings
topics.question: How could a story about Friends negotiating changed feelings develop conflict, consequences and a satisfying resolution?
topics.coverage: Primary context: Romance Stories; branch: Relationship stories. Address Friends negotiating changed feelings through one bounded case, source set or experiment. Exclude an all-purpose survey of the whole niche; distinguish the case's findings from broader claims.
research_outline: Define the protagonist's goal and the central conflict in Friends negotiating changed feelings.
Build three causally connected turning points with visible costs and character choices.
Plant a detail that earns the ending; test whether a reader can follow the world's rules.
Review cultural attribution, consent and sensitive portrayals; label the episode as original fiction.
topics.next_action: Select and inspect a concrete case and traceable sources; record unresolved questions before choosing a registered angle and promoting an episode idea.

media.requirements: Analyze an identifiable work or create a clearly labeled original example. Connect creative decisions to observable audience information; respect rights, attribution, consent and the difference between intent and reception.
source_leads: the actual work and authorized production materials
creator interviews or published craft explanations

fiction.requirements: Create original fiction with explicit world rules, character goals and causal continuity. Label invented events and separate inspiration from claims about actual cultures or living people.
source_leads: original story notes and world rules
reader feedback and a continuity audit

Choose one primary home for an actual episode and link it elsewhere. Where a subject appears in more than one context, retain the distinct case, population, system or interpretive question.

handoff: Keep the BANK ID in notes. Refine the research question with an exact text edition, jurisdiction, population, product version, place, time range or clearly labeled fictional premise.
Inspect actual sources; no source was verified by generating this map. Apply the existing registry planning and idea readiness process before project creation.
Choose a current registered angle only after reading its niche-specific scope. This initial map has not checked or assigned angle plans for these entries.
Keep Q1-Q42, CAT defaults, project snapshots, output locations and production gates unchanged. Catalog counts are not production or publication counts.
Review neighboring banks for semantic overlap and follow the existing Phase 1 claim-ledger requirements. Add qualified review when required by the production contract.
coverage_limits: This initial map does not exhaust the niche, its regions, time periods, named case studies, texts, technical variants or disputed questions. It has not performed source-feasibility checks, semantic duplicate review of every pair, trend analysis, claim verification or episode production. Expand any category freely after identifying a real coverage gap; add categories where the subject requires them. Preserve existing IDs when refining wording and allocate new IDs only for genuinely new proposals.
